idea.title: Plausible Analytics: privacy-friendly, cookie-free website analytics

source.text: Plausible Analytics: privacy-friendly, cookie-free website analytics, $6 per month, launch country EE (Estonia, selling worldwide online). Score it as of 2019-06-01: use only evidence published on or before that date (set verdict.as_of). Founder: two developers bootstrapping, side project. Just go: do not ask questions. Use the slug plausible-analytics.

idea.problem: Google Analytics is heavy, tracks visitors with cookies and personal data, and creates GDPR and cookie-consent burden for site owners.
idea.customer: Privacy-conscious indie developers, bloggers and small SaaS / agency site owners, mostly EU, who want simple traffic stats without cookie banners.
idea.solution: A lightweight, cookie-free hosted analytics script and one-page dashboard that collects no personal data.

context.edge: two developers who can build the product themselves

assumptions: Evaluated as of 2019-06-01 with evidence published on or before that date.
Budget assumed near zero (bootstrapped, under USD 1,000), hosting paid from pocket.
Time assumed 10-15 h per week per founder (side project).
Goal assumed side income first, with an option to go full-time.
No existing audience, mailing list or customers assumed.
Selling worldwide in English; Estonia is the legal base, not the main market.

confidence.note: Many numbers are estimates: no pre-2019-06 pricing pages for Fathom/Simple Analytics, no churn or CPC data. Archived pricing would raise it.

gross_margin.note: About **90%**: EUR 3.79/mo server and ~7% Stripe fee on a $6 plan; storage grows with pageviews.

ltv_cac.note: (estimate) LTV ~$90 vs organic CAC ~$40 = **2.25**; lifetime ~17 months at 6% churn.

pricing_power.note: GA is free on **55.7%** of sites; $6 undercuts paid peers, so price is set by the free anchor.

build_effort.note: Beta already live with 60+ users after ~2 months of building; paid plans only need billing.

skills_match.note: Developers building a developer tool; scaling event storage is the only hard part.

capital_needed.note: Near zero: a Hetzner CX11 costs EUR 3.79/month; no free tier keeps support cost down.

time_to_mvp.note: MVP exists (beta since Feb 2019); paid launch announced with pricing in April 2019.

sales_cycle.note: Self-serve card checkout; one person decides and pastes a script, same day.

channel_readiness.note: HN/Product Hunt launches proven for peers (Simple Analytics 40+ payers); no own audience.

search_demand.note: Active community demand: 'Migrating from Google Analytics' hit **352** HN points in Jan 2019.

trend.note: Rising: GDPR 2018, Safari ITP 2.1 (Feb 2019), 2 funded-by-customers peers launched in 2018.

willingness_to_pay.note: Peers charge, but proof is thin: Simple Analytics had ~$400 MRR from 40 customers.

free_alternatives.note: GA free, Matomo and Fathom open source; hosted convenience is the only paid gap. R5 cap.

competitor_density.note: Fathom and Simple Analytics launched 2018 for the same buyer, plus Matomo, GA, Clicky.

differentiation.note: Same pitch as Fathom and Simple Analytics (simple, private); only edge is a **lower price**.

legal_regulatory.note: IP is personal data (Breyer 2016); cookie-free avoids ePrivacy consent, but DPA work needed.

platform_dependency.note: Owns infra and data, but ad blockers (11% of users) may list the script and undercount.

market_risk.note: Durable, recurring need; privacy regulation is tightening, not a fad.

skills.note: Strong engineering; no marketing or sales track record in the evidence.

assets.note: No audience, list or network; 60 beta users are the only asset.

interest.note: Founder frames it as a privacy mission, but it runs as a side project.

tam.reasoning: 10M actively maintained small sites using an analytics tool x $72/year (12 x $6). Site count is an assumption; W3Techs gives shares, not counts.

sam.reasoning: 1% of TAM: privacy-conscious owners willing to pay for hosted analytics (assumption, anchored on Matomo's 1.2% share of sites).

som.reasoning: 1% of SAM in year 1 = ~1,000 customers at $6/month.

competitor_price_range.reasoning: Simple Analytics $400 MRR / 40 customers = ~$10 per customer; Fathom hosted price before 2019-06 not found.

variable_cost_per_unit.reasoning: Stripe 2.9% x 6 + EUR 0.25 (~$0.45) + hosting share ~$0.10 (EUR 3.79 box shared by ~40 small sites).

churn_monthly_pct.reasoning: Low-price subscription churn benchmark range ~5-7%/month (Recurly 2018 study); midpoint 6%.

conversion_rate_pct.reasoning: Launch-day visitors to paying: ~30-40 payers from ~30k HN visitors for a peer launch; assumed 0.1%.

cac.reasoning: Organic: ~40 founder hours of launch posts and content for ~30 customers = 1.3 h x $30/h value = ~$40.

fixed_costs_month.reasoning: 2-3 servers (EUR 3.79 each), backups, email and domain, accounting for an Estonian OU: ~$50/month.

break_even_customers_per_month.reasoning: 50 / 5.45 = 9.2, rounded up to 10 paying customers (costs only; no founder salary).

time_to_first_revenue_weeks.reasoning: Beta live with 60+ users and pricing announced (2019-04); converting beta users takes ~4 weeks.

verdict.launch_reason: Estonia is the legal base (0% tax on retained profits, EU company for GDPR trust); customers are sold worldwide in English.

rules_applied.effect: free_alternative hit: free_alternatives 2.5 -> 2; strong_competitor hit: competitor_density kept at 2.5 (<= 3)

type_checks.note: Low-price subscriptions churn ~5-7%/month (Recurly 2018 benchmarks, estimate range); a $6 plan needs volume to outrun churn. Shown in ltv_cac 2.5.
GA is free, on 55.7% of all sites, and its history is not portable; many users will run both tools before paying. Shown in pricing_power 2.

verdict.cheapest_test: Switch on paid plans for the 60+ beta users and post a Show HN the same week; count paying customers after 7 days.
kill_criteria: Fewer than 10 paying customers 7 days after paid launch and Show HN -> rework positioning before more building
Under $300 MRR by day 90 -> stop or change price/segment
Monthly churn above 10% in the first 3 months -> fix onboarding before marketing

rescue.change: Open-source the code (self-host free, hosted paid) and pitch it as transparent, EU-hosted analytics.
rescue.why: Fixes differentiation (2 -> 3) and turns GitHub into a channel (channel_readiness 3 -> 3.5, assets 1.5 -> 2).
rescue.requires: A licence choice (e.g. AGPL) and docs for self-hosting

rescue.change: Add a multi-site agency plan at $12-36/month and sell to EU web agencies needing GDPR-safe analytics.
rescue.why: Lifts pricing_power (2 -> 2.5) and willingness_to_pay (3 -> 3.5) with a higher ARPA buyer.
rescue.requires: Outbound sales time, a DPA template and agency features (client reports)

rescue.change: Make one founder full-time on content and SEO around 'Google Analytics alternative' and GDPR.
rescue.why: Builds an owned channel (channel_readiness 3 -> 3.5, assets 1.5 -> 2.5) instead of one launch spike.
rescue.requires: Writing skill and patience; savings to cover the income gap

narrative.answer: **PIVOT, 69/100**, one point short of GO. Cheap to build and run with ~90% margins and rising privacy demand, but Fathom and Simple Analytics launched the **same pitch** in 2018 and GA is free.
tldr: Unit economics work: ~90% gross margin, near-zero capital, self-serve sales.
Demand is real and rising (GDPR, Safari ITP 2.1, 352-point HN thread), but willingness to pay is barely proven.
Late third entrant with no edge but price; open-sourcing it is the cheapest way to stand out.

key_findings.title: Two look-alikes launched first in 2018
key_findings.detail: Fathom (Product Hunt #2, **2018-06**) and Simple Analytics (#3, 2018-09) sell the same simple, private analytics to the same indie buyers.

key_findings.title: Free Google Analytics anchors price at zero
key_findings.detail: GA runs on **55.7%** of all websites (W3Techs, 2019-01); Matomo and Fathom are free to self-host.

key_findings.title: Privacy demand is rising, proof of payment thin
key_findings.detail: A 'Migrating from Google Analytics' thread drew **352** HN points (2019-01), yet the best peer had ~$400 MRR from 40 customers.

narrative.recommendation: Launch paid plans now, but open-source the code and position it as transparent EU analytics; drop it if fewer than 10 beta users pay within 7 days.
narrative.steelman: Regulation (GDPR, ITP 2.1, CCPA) is pushing site owners off GA, the product is already built with 60+ beta users, and costs are so low that a few hundred customers is a profitable business. Evidence supports the tailwind and margins; it does not yet show demand beyond a few hundred dollars of MRR per player.

premortem.cause: Fathom and Simple Analytics own the niche; a cheaper copy gets no word of mouth.
premortem.early_signal: Fewer than 20 paying customers 30 days after the paid launch and Show HN.

premortem.cause: Free GA keeps buyers: users install it alongside GA, never pay, and leave after the trial.
premortem.early_signal: Trial-to-paid below 10% of the 60 beta users by day 30.

premortem.cause: Side-project hours stall marketing after the launch spike; MRR plateaus at a hobby level.
premortem.early_signal: New sign-ups fall under 5 per week after launch week.

changes.what: Safari ITP 2.1 caps client-side cookies at 7 days, breaking GA's returning-visitor counts; cookie-free tools are unaffected.
California signs CCPA, a second big privacy law after GDPR (2018-05), effective 2020.
The proposed ePrivacy Regulation would exempt only first-party audience measurement from consent.
CJEU Breyer: dynamic IP addresses can be personal data, raising GA's compliance burden.
Developers publicly migrate off GA, citing ad blockers and GDPR (352-point HN thread).

why_now.note: Regulation and browser changes in 2016-2019 opened the window, but 2 peers entered in 2018, so it is closing fast.

icp.who: Indie developers, bloggers and small SaaS founders (1-10 people), often in the EU, running 1-5 sites under 100k pageviews/month.
icp.pays_for_today: Mostly nothing (Google Analytics free); a few pay Fathom or Simple Analytics (~$10/month, estimate).
icp.budget: About $5-15/month per site (estimate from peer ARPA of ~$10).
icp.trigger: GDPR cookie-banner work, an ad blocker hiding their traffic, or a privacy stance on their own product.

free_alternative.evidence: Google Analytics is free on 55.7% of all sites (2019-01); Matomo (1.2%) and Fathom v1 (2018-05) are free open source.

strong_competitor.evidence: 3+ paid tools for the same buyer: Fathom (Product Hunt #2 of the day, 2018-06), Simple Analytics (#3, 2018-09; 40+ payers), Matomo (1.2% of all websites).

graveyard.evidence: Searched analytics shut-downs and post-mortems before 2019-06; no dated SaaS failure in this niche found.

no_distribution.evidence: Clear: HN and Product Hunt launches gave Simple Analytics 40+ paying customers; Plausible already has 60+ beta users from Indie Hackers.

costs_eat_margin.evidence: Clear: EUR 3.79/month server and ~7.5% Stripe fees leave ~90% gross margin on $6.

weak_demand.evidence: Clear: 352-point HN thread on leaving GA (2019-01) and a 284-point thread (2019-03) show rising demand.

legal_platform_risk.evidence: Clear with work: cookie-free avoids ePrivacy consent, but IPs are personal data (Breyer, 2016) and ad blockers (11% of users) may block the script.

saturated_wave.evidence: Clear: 3 near-identical launches found (Fathom, Fathom PRO, Simple Analytics) in 2018-06 to 2019-06, under the 10 threshold.

customer.segment: Privacy-minded indie developers and small site owners
customer.pain: GA is heavy, needs a cookie banner under EU rules and is blocked by ad blockers.
customer.today: Google Analytics for free, self-hosted Matomo, or ~$10/month Fathom / Simple Analytics.

use_cases.name: Indie blog and SaaS landing-page stats without a cookie banner
Agency running GDPR-safe analytics for many client sites

competitors.name: Google Analytics
competitors.gap: Cookies, consent banner, heavy UI, blocked by ad blockers

competitors.name: Fathom Analytics
competitors.traction_note: Product Hunt #2 of the day (2018-06); open source v1 + hosted PRO (2018-09)

competitors.name: Simple Analytics
competitors.gap: Closed source; price ~$10 (estimate from MRR / customers)

competitors.name: Yandex.Metrica
competitors.gap: Session recording and tracking, worse on privacy than GA

fact_checks.evidence: True if raw IPs are never stored: under Breyer (2016) a dynamic IP can be personal data.
No cookies means ePrivacy art. 5(3) consent should not apply; WP194 says analytics cookies do need consent.
The April 2019 launch post describes a solo founder; a second person is not in evidence before 2019-06.

scenarios.name: Pessimistic
scenarios.note: Only part of the beta converts; churn 8%

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.note: Show HN + content; 6% churn; $0.55 variable + $50 fixed

scenarios.name: Optimistic
scenarios.note: Mix shifts to $12 plans after open-sourcing; HN front page

risks.risk: Ad-block lists (EasyPrivacy) add the script domain, undercounting customers' traffic
risks.mitigation: Custom-domain proxy option for the script

risks.risk: ePrivacy Regulation final text drops or narrows the analytics exemption
risks.mitigation: Stay cookie-free, store no IPs, offer a DPA

risks.risk: Fathom or Simple Analytics cuts price to $5 or adds a free tier
risks.mitigation: Compete on openness and EU hosting, not price

risks.risk: Side-project time stalls support and features
risks.mitigation: Set a revenue target that triggers going full-time

test_plan.step: Turn on billing and email the 60+ beta users with the 1/3 beta discount
Post a Show HN and an Indie Hackers update with the open-source repo
Reply to every comment; collect objections versus Fathom and Simple Analytics
Count paying customers and trial starts
test_plan.verify: 10+ paying customers -> keep going; fewer -> rework positioning
